subject: rstan install no-go, mac os x yosemite

messages.author: d2ca95393bc23535
messages.subject: rstan install no-go, mac os x yosemite
parts:
Hi,
I'm having trouble installing rstan; I just updated to OS X Yosemite to get clang compilers, updated to R 3.2.0, uninstalled rstan, checked the dependencies, so Rcpp and inline are working just fine.

When I run the install_stan() script I get:

fatal error: too many errors emitted, stopping now [-ferror-limit=]
20 errors generated.
make: *** [gm__grammars__functions_grammar_inst.o] Error 1
ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘rstan’

----------------------
The full echo'd output with all the errors in detail is attached as a zip.

---------------------
sessionInfo() gives:

R version 3.2.0 (2015-04-16)
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin13.4.0 (64-bit)
Running under: OS X 10.10.3 (Yosemite)

locale:
[1] en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] Rcpp_0.11.5   inline_0.3.14

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] tools_3.2.0 tcltk_3.2.0

--------------------------
my .R/Makevars looks like this:

# created by rstan at Thu Dec  4 02:32:00 2014 
CXXFLAGS = -mtune=core2 -O3 $(LTO)  #set_by_rstan
R_XTRA_CPPFLAGS =  -I$(R_INCLUDE_DIR)   #set_by_rstan
CC=clang
CXX=clang++ -arch x86_64 -ftemplate-depth-256
--------------------------

Thanks for making a nice piece of software for the community.
Edward

messages.subject: Re: rstan install no-go, mac os x yosemite
parts:
Ben,
Thank you, so the problem is caused by incompatible boost versions. I have the R package BH version 1.55.0-3, i.e. Boost 1.55, and in /usr/local/include I have boost version 1.57.

Unfortunately I don't understand how to fix this so rstan installs. Is there a line I should comment out or uncomment? Need I upgrade or downgrade BH or boost?

Thank you for your help, and for your patience.
Edward

On Tuesday, April 21, 2015 at 11:26:40 PM UTC-5, Ben Goodrich wrote:

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan install no-go, mac os x yosemite
parts:
Do you know what causes things like

-I/usr/local/include -I/usr/local/include/freetype2 -I/opt/X11/include -mtune=core2 -g etc.

to be added to the CFLAGS? The intent of all those lines about R_MAKEVARS_USER and R_MAKEVARS_SITE in install_rstan() is to avoid all that but somehow it is slipping through.

Ben

messages.author: d2ca95393bc23535
messages.subject: Re: rstan install no-go, mac os x yosemite
parts:
I'm not sure, but I'd bet on homebrew. I have Homebrew 0.9.5 as a package manager, and that might set global CFLAGS/CPPFLAGS. Alternatively it could be xquartz given x11 is in there. 

How do I tell what my CPPFLAGS are set to (expertise fail and google fail on my end)?
Edward

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan install no-go, mac os x yosemite
parts:
In the Terminal app (under Applications/Utilities) you can do

R CMD config CXXFLAGS

but that is only going to tell us what they are rather than what is responsible for putting them there.

You could downgrade your local Boost to 1.55 but you shouldn't have to do that.

Ben

messages.author: d2ca95393bc23535
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstan install no-go, mac os x yosemite
parts:
What worked to install stan (tested on the 8schools example) was to add the line to ~/.R/Makevars
CPPFLAGS  = 

and then to run:
devtools::install_url("https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases/download/v2.6.0/rstan_2.6.0.tar.gz")

I think I had tried both of those independently, but they only worked together.

Thank you all for the suggestions and help.
Edward
